name: Wik-Epa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct; Sutton & Hale 2021:129 treat Wik-Ep (=Wik-Iit) only as a dialect label under Wik-Me'nh with no phonological description; no grammar or sketch located.

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter & Ken Hale. 2021. Linguistic Organisation and Native Title: The Wik Case, Australia. Canberra: ANU Press (Asia-Pacific Linguistics). doi:10.22459/LONT.2021. Ch.7 'Wik Subgroup grammatical history' (Hale, written 1997), pp.177-220; ch.6 pp.133-136; ch.5 p.129; ch.3 p.58.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p.181 (Hale, section 'Wik-Me'nh (Me) and Wik-Mungkan (Mn) pronominals'; Hale's 'Me' = 'Wik Me'nh, Wik Ep', Hale notes 1960, p.135-136): free pronouns 'carry stress or accent', dependent pronouns are 'unstressed (atonic)' enclitics; Wik-Me'nh, Wik-Mungkan, Wik-Ngathan, Wik-Ngatharr have undergone 'reduction of unstressed post-consonantal vowels—i.e. unstressed vowels in the V-position of CV syllables' (all non-first-syllable vowels omitted in his orthography). Implies word-initial stress but never states where word stress falls. p.182 fn.5 (Sutton): first-syllable vowel is 'the vowel with prim…

sources.citation: Sutton, Peter. 1978. Wik: Aboriginal society, territory and language at Cape Keerweer, Cape York Peninsula, Australia. PhD thesis, University of Queensland. (ANU Open Research text bundle, hdl:1885/307607)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress statement (App.1 p.236: 'primary stress falls on the first vowel of any word') is for Wik-Ngathana only. On Wik-Epa: pp.37-40 Wik-Epa = Wik-Iita, dialect of clans 10 and 13, 'most similar to' Wik-Me'anha; Hale 1960 'Wik Ep or Wik Me?n, ms'; ch.IV: Ep is extinct and the clan-10 dialect 'has not yet been recorded' (Hale's data came from a clan-13 speaker whose dialect is called both Ep and Me); Nr, Nn, Me, Ep share /oe, ooe/ and word-final neutral vowel reanalysis. No stress statement for Ep/Me.
